explanation: The E138A mutation reduces rilpivirine binding through an indirect allosteric mechanism rather than direct contact. The negatively charged glutamate at position 138 is located ~43 Å from the NNRTI pocket, and its replacement with small, neutral alanine eliminates a critical electrostatic anchor point that stabilizes the overall three-dimensional architecture of the palm domain; loss of this negative charge removes an organizing electrostatic influence that maintains the precise geometric presentation of rilpivirine-binding residues. The 50 Ų volume reduction coupled with the loss of negative charge likely permits localized conformational relaxation in the NNRTI-binding pocket, destabilizing favorable van der Waals and electrostatic complementarity with the inhibitor despite the direct contact points remaining geometrically intact.
